reviews.comment: pretty good professor in the beginning of the course, gradually decreased a little towards the end. he has online lecture notes he teaches off of, and there is clear examples for the material and his quizzes. the lectures are difficult to follow though because he goes a little fast in derivations in the theoretical parts.

Exams make up a decent amount of your grade in the class, but grading is lenient and lots of partial credit. Lectures are sometimes confusing, but overall pretty good. There is no homework but rather weekly quizzes which are easy to prepare for since he gives you questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor for first 2 exams, but for some reason fell off when it came to reviewing for the final. There was almost no prep questions for the final, unlike the first two, so be prepared to study a lot by yourself. He does give exam reviews however.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I got a C in DiffEq proceeded to get an A in this class. So helpful and a great lecturer. Also has a ton of youtube videos to help, and super good at answering emails/dumb questions. Probably the best Math prof I had from my entire set of Math minor classes.

Amazing professor, this class is like drinking water. Generous/lenient grader. Teaches with board and marker which is the best way in my opinion. One of the few teachers who actually give a review day before the exam. The bad reviews are probably from engineers, since everyone knows engineers hate math. Funny guy as well.

Class wasn't too hard. I maintained an A in the class up until the final, where I fumbled and got a 70%. This dropped my grade to an 89.7% and he refused to round up, so I got a B. Overall a chill guy but it sucked that this was the only B I've gotten in my A&M career.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He no longer has homework and you are graded by quizzes and exams. that may sound like you wont learn or understand enough but that isn't the case. he makes the quizes really easy if you do his prep questions and the exams are pretty similar to the quizzes. good class

I honestly struggled a lot in this class because I didn't have any background in precal, trig, or calc. But I made it a priority to attend the MLC every chance I could. Landon and Isa are incredible tutors and helped SO MUCH. (I was also lucky to have a great TA). While I often had trouble understanding Rahm's lectures, he was always kind. STUDY!

I'm not sure why his ratings are bad. He is a really good lecturer, albeit can be a little speedy some times. He always answers questions, even some really stupid ones. Homework is pretty helpful and not overly lengthy. He's pretty generous with partial credit on the exams. Posts his completed notes on canvas which is also helpful.

Look, rahm is a great guy, there's no doubt. I just think math140 is a terrible class and no one has a good experience with it. He did his best the material he had, but our class average was terrible. He's a nice and smart dude- I just think he didn't want to be there and he is likely better in the advanced math that he actually cares about.

The class was a blur. It was so difficult to understand what he was saying because he'd ramble. His explanations were so complex & feedback was useless. Even in office hours, he'd ignore us & simply asked to try again when stuck. Exams looked for small rules that didn't test learning but mere test-taking & random tidbits of information. Avoid him.

This class put me through hell and back. I showed up, I tried, I cried, and all I got in return was stress and bad grades. It drained every ounce of energy I had. If you love yourself even a little bit and value your peace, time, and sanity, do NOT take this class. Take it at a community college and transfer the credit.
This guy yaps more than teaches
Tests were extremely difficult and covered topics discussed minimally in class. I took Calculus in high school and got a 98, but got a C in Rahm's class despite devoting way more time to it.

I did not take calculus in high school and I finished with a 97 in this class. To succeed: DO THE TEXTBOOK PRACTICE PROBLEMS, they are insanely helpful. Also, attend recitation and make sure to ask questions. His lectures can be confusing, but the text book, hw and quizzes make it clear what the exams will be like.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rahm goes very fast in his lectures and his hand writing is hard to read. He's super chill though. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you don't show up to lectures you're gonna be completely lost. Not a whole lot of homework, but does in class quizzes. Definitely just rework homework problems a lot until you understand the material.

I genuinely don't know how I survived his class, the exams were horrible. Really the only way you can get an A is if you have taken calc before. Exams are 80% of your grade and mostly FRQ make sure to go to the math learning center before them. Office hours don't help. The only thing I was looking forward to in the course was writing this review.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have taken Calc in the past you should be better of than people who have not. Lectures are hard to understand and he makes everything over complicated when it is easy in reality. Utilize the math learning center A LOT they are very helpful and make sure to do your best in class quizzes, projects, and homework as they are easier assignments.

Prof Rahm can be tricky to follow in lectures, but the recitation sections are super helpful. Definitely take advantage of those and the free textbook. unstuck ai was a lifesaver for practice problems too. Overall, put in the work and you can succeed in this course.

People on here love to complain. Prof Rahm was one of the best professors I had all semester. I came out of the class with a far deeper, conceptual understanding of Calculus, and genuinely found the class so enjoyable that I strongly considered taking Calc 2 despite being pre-med. Take this class if you want to learn how to think!!

Don't skip class, take notes, and don't try to email him for any sort of extra credit.     Dr. Rahm was nice and happy to help with questions after/before lecture. Also had weekly quizzes during recitation. But if you don't actually have to take 147 and can do 140/142 instead, definitely don't pick this class!

If you are not a good test taker, GOOD LUCK. Good professor, but can be confusing in class. Test heavy class and is very easy to get a B on tests as each mcq is like worth 6 points. GO TO CLASS. Nice professor and easy to talk to. Do the hw and review problems, u should be fine. No extra credit.

Before I say anything I would like to clarify Calculus has always been something im awful at and the fact i even got an A in his class amazes me, first of all Professor Rahm is not an awful professor, calculus is an awful class in general for many pre-meds. i for one did not expect to get an A but professor Rahm made it very clear how to study.

Do NOT take this prof. Lectures are fast, confusing, and prone to many errors. Dissertation was the only reason I passed. 147 will consume your time and drain your livelihood. Even the people that took calc in high school shed tears. There're two projects that are easy As, and he subs your lowest exam, but that's all the kindness he spares. AVOID.

If you do the homework you should be fine for the exams. Final drops lowest test grade so they'res no need to worry if you bomb one. Take this prof if you have prior calc knowledge and you should be well off

Dr. Rahm is a very nice and caring guy, but he should consider a new profession because he is an awful teacher. He constantly made careless errors in his lecture notes and his grading. If you have the option- do not take math 147 with Dr. Rahm. The material itself is not too difficult- but he makes it 100x more confusing than it really is.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute goat when it came to helping us prepare for exams and learn the material. Told us what to expect and honestly carried.
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If possible do not take him! I took calculus in high school so everything was mostly review. His lectures aren't helpful at all, he goes extremely fast, makes TONS of errors during lecture and while grading exams. TBH only go to recitation and watch YouTube videos on what isn't reviewed in recitation. Also doing textbook problems is very helpful.

His lectures are hard to follow because he moves through the content EXTREMELY FAST, but the plus is that he does a thorough job of ensuring that he covers all the cases of a new topic so you know how to do the homework and the test. I've never had to look up stuff on yt because his posted notes are so thorough. Take the time to study the notes.

The class isn't the best because you dont know what type of questions you are going to get in the tests. The only thing you will know from the review is to practice some questions that will just be a good for foundation. But you won't know what the test will be like at all. Recitations have similar type of questions asked in the test so go to those

Very straightforward class. He is a good prof and his office hours are helpful. 3 tests 20% each and if you do the review questions from the book, you will do well. Tests are mostly frq. Quiz every Friday which is worth 5% total and very easy if you do the hw. If you slack off you will get behind and it will be harder.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is alright, since he is very funny yet disorganized with his lectures. It is easy to get lost. GO TO RECITATIONS! It is extremely helpful. If you taken Calc in HS then you will be fine. Exams are tricky. Avoid him if allowed.

Kinda nice dude but isn't good at all in lecturing. Backtracks often and doesn't explain topics clearly. A good bit of homework but is easy to do. Only a few new topics for students already experienced in calculus. Recitation is much more helpful as you do actual practice. There are often mistakes while grading and mistakes on exam questions. AVOID

Took Calc AB before? You'll be good. How to get an A: Get the textbook online and ACTUALLY do EVERY question listed on the study guides bc tests aren't curved + are 85% of your grade (but every problem on the test has one like it in those sets). GO TO RECITATION!! Material itself isn't too complicated but moves fast, so go to the MLC for extra help
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rahm is the worst lecturer ever. He writes more paragraphs in notes than solving actual problems. I had to do over 100 questions (WHICH HE ASSIGNED) before each exam to even semi understand the material, only for the test to be totally different and purely made of weird applications. This class is a doable at a cost to ur time and overall happiness
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ask him questions about his course and he is open ended and almost useless. He's not there for you, he's there to teach his class. D head at the end of semester, did not even consider the option of any curve or round up from a 68, and called my email asking for one nicely "inappropriate".I've sat through worse lectures, but do not like this guy.

Literally the worst class i've had the misfortune of experiencing. Lectures are so conceptual and theoretical you basically waste an hour of your life. Tests literally make or break your grade, and the only practice material provided is the textbook, which is nothing similar to exam questions. If I could time travel I'd go back and fail my MPE.

Professor Rahm was genuinely the epitomy of what a terrible professor is. His lectures make no sense and are nearly impossible to follow, he's extremely difficult to reach outside of class and tries to act oblivious to the fact that people dislike him. Despite taking Calc BC in high school, I had to put a crazy amount of effort into this class.

I would never recommend this professor to anyone ever again. He spends mosts of his time in class explaining stuff that doesn't even matter for the actual tests and quizzes. He just wastes time expelling the proof of calculus that doesn't even help for anything. If I were you I would just go to the recitations and ask all my questions.

Dr. Rahm is an awful teacher. His lectures are all over the place and they don't correlate with recitation, quizzes, homework, or the textbook. If I hadn't taken calc in high school I would NOT take this class. Also tests are literally 85% of the grade sooooo don't take him. Also don't 147 in general, take 140/142 or ANY other calc.

Weekly quizzes make up 5% of your grade, so pay attention in recitation because the tests are full of mistakes. No extra credit at all. Two projects are your only hope for a grade boost. No practice exams, just a lousy study guide. Lectures are useless because he's terrible at explaining. Challenging if you haven't taken calc before.

If you dont have any Calc knowledge, dont take him. He doesnt know how to teach. For exams, he has a list of questions that he tells you should know. But, on the exam, forget it, they're two completely different things. I can't tell you how much I hated his class. His exams are hard, but he does curve since everyone does awful. Dont take him

Rahm has never given out answer keys to any of our tests, which makes it difficult to see how to solve the problems we missed. Reviews are only based on textbook problems, which differ greatly from those given on the exams. I wouldn't be surprised if he has to curve our final grade significantly. He is a nice guy but he is not a great teacher.
I'm writing this two years after taking this god awful class. It still keeps me up at night. Take someone else if you love yourself and value your life.
Does not grade consistently and overcomplicates everything. Do NOT take this class at all.
Takes long to grade exams and never grades them consistently. I took Calculus in high school and he over complicates things and does not grade the same for everyone. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!

This class is incredibly doable if you take the time to prepare. Prof Rahm makes it clear that you need to put in a decent deal of work outside of class in order to be successful. Listen to the advice he gives because he tells you how to succeed.

I agree with the reviews saying that the course would have been much harder if you didn't take calculus in high school already. Although I don't recommend him as an IDEAL choice for new calc students it also isn't impossible. If you got him randomly assigned you'll most likely be fine but if you haven't taken calc and want an A take someone else.

Literally do NOT take him if you have no background in calculus. He is chill but makes everything SO much more complicated and the TAs literally taught better than him. You are literally going to struggle because he cannot teach and is honestly not even that helpful when you ask questions. 3 exams+1 final worth 85% and 1 homework/week.

DO NOT TAKE HIM!! If you did not do AP Calculus in high school, I would highly suggest just taking this class at a community college. I am not good at math, and he did not make it any easier. His lectures were very confusing, he would even confuse himself. He overcomplicated everything when it shouldn't have been.

He's really funny but not good at teaching AT ALL. Don't take if you haven't taken AP calculus. He overcomplicates everything and explains proofs when all you need are equations. Rahm isn't trying to make people fail though so problems are easy if you understand. Self-studying or learning from recitation and using class to reinforce got me the A+.
RUN AS FAR AS POSSIBLE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Jeez, people are really harsh on him. Calculus is hard. At the beginning of the year he tells you that to be successful you have to put in a lot of time into learning. He gives practice problems from the textbook, tells you what to study, and it very flexible in the exam.

Exams are predominantly multiple choice. I liked him, honestly.
Would NOT recommend.

He goes in circles during lectures and isn't the best at explaining concepts. Exams are annoyingly 85% of the grade.. However, he cares about his students and is nice. Make sure to read chapters before class, answer all the practice problems in the text book and go to every recitation. I got an A in this class with no prior calculus knowledge.

He only writes notes on whiteboards in class- so you can't miss it!! He teaches everything way more complicated than necessary. I dropped the class and the new professor I have makes the material so simple. Rahm insisted on making everything ridiculously conceptual when not needed. He also gave a study guide and no material from it was on the exam.

Attendance isn't technically mandatory but you're shooting yourself in the foot if you don't go. Material is dense but manageable; the biggest issue by far are exams. Apart from a slight curve on one test, what you get is what's going on your transcript. Grading is extremely harsh - small errors will often lose you the whole question.

Does not post any notes. You have to show up to lecture to get your own notes. Lectures can be confusing as he tends to make things more complicated than they need to be. A lot of conceptual questions on homeworks but exams have no conceptual questions. Have to know a lot calculus stuff like a lot of integrals and trig identities

Lectures are fine, sometimes he can be a little disorganized tho. Homework once a week and typically arent that hard. Exams suck tho. imo exams werent hard, just way too long. Genuinely knew the content but only did about 3/5 of the test before running out of time. Multiple questions on exams would be whole pages of calculations which took so long

Bad lecturer. Lectures are on whiteboard and feel rushed. Test 1 is easy. Test 2 average was like 60 then he curved 10 points. Homework is fine, but doesnt cover everything on the tests. Gives study guide for test that is just topics and no problems, so he assigns optional problems from the textbook. He chill, but would not recommend.

His lectures are more theory based than practice problem based, which means you have to put in work outside of class for a good grade. His exams aren't super difficult if you prepare well for them but you have to put in a lot of work. Overall he is a cool guy and pretty understanding.

Show up to lecture, take notes, and ask questions. MATH251 is not a class you can sleep through, but if you participate and pay attention, Rahm's teaching style works. He is also great about answering questions. 

Also, Paul's Online Math Notes work great as a supplemental material.

Do not take this professor, he is absolutely horrible at teaching. He just yaps the whole entire class and teaches you stuff that you do not need to know. Makes things more complicated than it actually is.

Calculus is a tough subject for me but prof Rahm made it a lot better. Following him in lectures can be tricky at times because he tends to skip steps but is very open to questions and will happily go over anything you need. Quizzes every Friday and hw due 1/2 times per week. 2 projects that were super easy almost impossible to not get 100 on.

Took him for math251. He is a nice guy and wants us to do well, very funny and easy to talk to but hes very unorganized. Came to class every day with notes in his hands so we had nothing to access outside of class. He is hard to follow at times and just overall not the easiest. He has good test reviews so that is nice but overall take someone else.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Please, I implore you, do not take this Professor. If he is the only one available when registering, take the class next semester with a different professor and take Stats 201 instead. He is disorganized in his lectures and barely teaches a subject, then expects you to know everything about it. The TA taught better than him. DO NOT TAKE!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher, and the only way that I was able to end with an A is because I took AP calc in high school. All of my friends who didn't had to q-drop. He is horrible at explaining things, explains things in the most complicated way possible, and just does not care about his students. He is not accessible and hardly responds to emails. hated.

Sometimes he gets REALLY into showing how to derive the proof for something that he spends the whole class on it. I did the homework during class. Recitation helped SO much more than lecture did, attend every single one that you can. He does not give practice exams but there's 2 "projects" that are pretty simple and were a nice grade boost.

Rob teaches at a very fast pace. This is not a class you can do well in without a lot of practice outside of class. He is a great prof though and makes class entertaining. He forgets to post quizzes sometimes and then you don't have to do them. There are not a lot of online resources provided but he allows you to use whatever you want online.
Gets so lost in the lecture. Do not take. The TA will save you.
He is really bad at explaining things. Will overcomplicate absolutely everything.

HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE
Amazing professor that actually teaches and makes jokes.

He's a funny guy but does not know how to teach MATH 147. His lectures make me even more confused than I already am. As someone who didn't take calc in high school, this class has put me through hell and back. The questions on the test are nothing like what's taught in class. His homeworks are fine. Honestly my TA teaches the class better,

He is one of the worst professors for math. He expects every student to already know what he is teaching. He switches topics every 2 minuets and is just overall disorganized. His email turn around is 8+ business days which isn't helpful especially when you need help. Went to office hours to ask questions and he acted as if I wasn't there.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Okay listen, he isn't a bad teacher. He explains what he is supposed to, but not enough that people understand what he is saying. This really just stems from how disorganized his lecture is. He himself isn't a bad guy, and it is clear he knows his math, but he fumbles around a lot. Overall, he is just super out of order, but willing to help.
bad

Dr. Rahm is a gem. Online summer classes are hard enough without being 400 level math classes, but he made it entirely manageable. The tests were over zoom, not take home, but that was fine. He was very accessible and kind even when hard stuff happens that should ruin his day. Put in the work and learn how to use latex for hw and you'll be golden.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: do not take him ever. extremely unorganized, constantly switching between different topics and usually doesnt explain why he is doing something. doesnt post notes, only the textbook with questions but it doesnt tell you how to solve them. if youre stuck with him go to recitations. material on tests is not taught in class.

Professor Rahm genuinely does not know how to teach. The tests are nothing like the material he goes over in class, on the study guides, or on the homework. He does not know how to explain the subjects to people who have not taken calculus before and basically expects EVERYONE to already know what we are doing.

His lectures are hard to follow because he bounces around from topic to topic. Go to recitations if you can because often times the TAs are easier to understand than he is. He's a funny guy who loves math, but he also gets mad at the lecture hall when we don't follow his explanations...

By whatever means possible do not take this professor. He was notorious for giving confusing instructions and not making any sense. I cannot name a single person who also took his class that wasn't confused. Messes up during lectures and you end up having to teach yourself everything. If you do end up being stuck with him utilize MLC.

Professor Rahm is very disorganized, so if you don't study outside of class, you will not perform well. My biggest gripe is that quizzes are 1 question in 5 minutes, so if your TA doesn't explain the content well, you will perform badly. Rahm is funny and cares about his students, but the class is difficult and his disorganization doesn't help.

Math 412 is not an easy class but Dr. Rahm was able to explain difficult concepts and provided a lot of problems to practice which were really useful for the exams. While his notes are disorganized, he puts in a lot of effort into creating them for the class. He provided extra credit on every homework assignment which helped me with my grade

152 is a weed-out course so its already going to be tough. Rahm didn't do a good job of teaching it. He always uploaded the notes for the lecture the day-of, which was annoying. 152 uses common exams so other professor's notes from friends were very helpful. Also, you have 1 quiz a week that is 5 minutes long. Try to get someone else if you can.

He doesn't make any sense explaining any of the concepts related to math 152 because he's talking way too fast and rushing through the examples. He goes so fast to the point where he messed up countless times in examples which derailed any semblance of the lesson for that day.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: inefficient and unorganized notes. he didn't proofread his questions and would have to modify the questions every class. terrible lectures, explains everything super confusing. makes an already difficult weedout class impossible to learn without any outside resources. Lots of outside of class time and resources is the only way to survive. dont take

Rob says that you need to do at least 40-80 extra practice problems a week to do well (to compensate for his "teaching" and "notes" tbh). Also, you have to teach yourself everything before lecture to understand him because he's so confusing and goes incredibly fast. I started skipping and my grade went from a D to a B. Joe Kahlig's notes saved me.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: - UNORGANIZED - horrible, unlabeled notes - changes notes every other day - makes a LOT of mistakes during lectures - lowkey funny - teaches too fast - spends time doing proofs rather than helpful problems. You probably didn't have a choice but read the textbook before class, do the hw on time, and hope you get a good TA. MLC and HOGU were helpful.

This prof is perfect if you already know the material before his lectures. I'm not one of them (my first time learning Calc 2). The instant you get deeply lost, his lectures becomes increasingly hard to follow. Additionally, he should post his lecture notes before class starts more often.

Math is not my thing, so being in math class is not my favorite, but Dr. Rahm was funny and easy to talk to. Lectures were a little fast but manageable. Plus the notes were posted after class anyway - so you don't have to attend lecture! Mistakes in lectures were small and he didn't hesitate to be corrected.
Bro wasted my time and hardly ever actually taught. When he did, went ENTIRELY too fast and used confusing methods for teaching. Waste of time. Don't take Rahm.

-Frequently makes mistakes when teaching the material, becomes flustered when he realizes mistakes
-Clearly doesn't have a firm grasp on the material (admitted to scoring an 85 on the first exam of the sem.)
-Unfairly quizzes students on material taught the day before the quiz despite lecture notes not being uploaded
-1 question quizzes weekly

He is super caring and genuinely wants his students to succeed. However, he gets flustered easily while lecturing and makes many mistakes with simple arithmetic. He has some crazy stories. One time he brought his kid to class. If you already know what's going on, it's kind of fun to watch the chaos evolve; if you're struggling do not take him.

I really liked Professor Rahm's class, but it was quite fast paced as there is a lot of material covered in the class. The homework every week was some short questions from provided videos, several sets of equations, and a short "quiz" every Friday. He dropped several low grades and the final will take the place of your lowest exam score as well.

The lectures are entertaining, but they aren't helpful. The notes constantly change, meaning the packet he uses on Monday won't be the same packet he uses later in the week. The first exam had an average of 67.3. With regrade requests (students catching grading mistakes on their exams) the average went up to a 69. DON'T TAKE HIM

-Frequent mistakes during lecture (gets flustered and has to check his own notes or Desmos to find the correct solution)
-Barely explains the concepts
-"Teaches" at lightning speed
-Skips too many steps in his examples
-1 question quizzes over content you learned in the previous lecture (Thursday's quiz WILL go over Wednesday's lecture content)

I have Rahm for Math 152 this year. The class itself is already hard and Rahm's lecture increase that difficulty ten fold. I would recommend taking a different professor for calculus 2 because Rahm is not it.

Professor Rahm is a funny guy and you can tell he genuinely cares about us. He isn't the best lecturer because he likes to go fast, but he goes back to re-explain if someone didn't understand a topic. He drops a bunch of your lowest grades. Tests are all open-ended with partial credit. How you perform on the tests will likely determine your grade.

Rahm was a great guy but not a great teacher. There was a work load but not too heavy. All of the other teachers gave multiple choice tests with enough time but we didn't have multiple choice and there was never enough time to complete the tests. Also he says he gives partial credit but he grades super tough and doesn't really give partial credit.

Rahm is a wonderful guy, but I would not recommend him. Most of the other math140 teachers give mcq tests with more time, while ours were free response with not enough time. The pace is fast and I struggled to keep up. I always studied for tests and felt good abt them but then received a C or low B, while my friends in other classes were chillin

Professor Rahm is a hilarious teacher. I enjoyed taking his class but his lectures are very fast, so If you're not a fast learner I would recommend taking another teacher. But if you learn fast I would recommend him since the workload is not that much and his class just consists of group quizzes on friday's and tests.

Rahm is a nice, funny guy. His lectures can be a lot to comprehend considering his smartness, but he is always willing to help and helpful during office hours. The homework can sometimes be a lot but that's for any math class. He could probably do better, but he's overall a good professor if you go to class and do the work.

Professor Rahm is a good guy. He reviews the notes posted online in lecture and does examples, but he goes through a new topic pretty quickly. Quite a bit of homework but manageable. Lots of opportunities for getting grades (weekly "group" quizzes, homeworks, video quizzes) but tests are free response, so you either know the material or you don't.

Professor Rahm does a good job of teaching Math 140, however, it's necessarily an easy course. There's quite a bit of homework and studying is definitely mandatory. The tests are all free response but he gives partial credit. He is also one of the funniest teachers I have ever had.

Rob Rahm is very smart and kinda awkward but he really cares about the success of his students. He is always open to answer questions and he is just a super chill and cool dude. Tests are all free response. Test are very straight-forward and if you know the material you will be successful.

Rahm is definitely one of the better 140 professors. He isn't the best teacher, but very caring and will help if you need it. There is a decent amount of homework, but all classes will have the same. As long as you stay on top of things you will be fine. Recommend him!

He is a very caring person, but his lectures are not very concise. He frequently makes mistakes and doesn't know where numbers come from in his work. He gets jumbled up and loses his train of thought. He is not very accessible outside of class, but overall is a very nice professor.

Rahm is a very nice guy, but a very scattered lecturer. He makes mistakes and jumps around which makes understanding difficult. Thankfully, the content in the class wasn't too challenging. The class has so many grades, and attendance is not mandatory, but he did some Clicker questions for grades in class. Weekly group work was sometimes difficult.

Rob is the best math teacher you're going to find for Math 140. Although he is not ideal for everyone, he is so much better than the other teachers. The work is not crazy - you will have homework assignments due every week, but homework is inevitable. Rob is an easier grader than the other professors and he honestly makes the class enjoyable.

This guy is very smart,  but im not sure that translates to his teaching. People who have taken the course before in highschool or already understand the concepts do well, but if youre not one of those people, youre toast. You have to teach yourself with the lecture videos from the annoying lady and the textbook that is $30

for Spring 2020:
Rahm seemed like a nice guy, but he was a very scattered and flustered lecturer. He responded terribly to questions in class; was v. condescending. Frequently made mistakes in lectures and took little notice or responsibility. The lectures did not correlate to the online hw, which did not correlate to the exams. Would not rec.

A good person but not that great of a professor. His lectures are often boring and confusing, especially given that Calc II is way harder than Calc I. Occasionally confuses himself when going over the subject material. There's some extra credit but it's not going to help too much if you struggle on the tests, which I did a lot during this semester.

Dr. Rahm is an amazing person but not the best professor. Calculus II is already very difficult, and he doesn't make it any easier to learn the concepts. You have to read the textbook to do well! He is always willing to help outside of class though, and it was awesome getting to know him. If he gives extra credit, do it (it helps tremendously)!!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Robert is a good fella but his lectures can be a bit boring, unclear, and confusing many times. The class is very difficult as is since we are required to understand the proofs being taught but Robert doesn't make it much easier to understand them. The homework isn't too bad, but the tests are difficult as hell. There is extra credit so take it

So I took this prof in fall 2021, He is not good. I would not take him at all. He spends the entire lecture proving stuff rather than working on problems and actually showing the concepts. Beware, the tests are not like the past exams. The Coding part of the class was fine but the lectures were awful. If you have him then look at week-in-reviews!

Professor Rahm is a genuine guy that cares a lot about his students. However, his lectures are not always helpful because he believes that proofs are necessary to teach students the material but more often than not they confuse the class. Furthermore, he also stopped posting the notes on time around midway through the semester.

Nice, decent guy. When I attended lecture I had a good time. I wouldn't say his lectures are vital though, one would benefit more from the week-in-reviews than actual lecture. His TA this semester was great, I definitely recommend always going to recitation/lab and to Rahm's lecture during test review week for extra help and review. Good prof.

Rahm has a good personality but his lectures were pretty much useless to me. He would only be able to get through the beginning of the lesson so wed be left with self teaching most of the homework. I feel like he lectures too fast and assumes we know more than we do.
Cooperative

Dr. Rahm is a standup guy who seems to really appreciate his students and his work. I sometimes found myself learning more outside of class than inside, and making sure to attend WIR (Week-In-Review) sessions is key. Dr. Rahm is a decent choice for a difficult class.

Rahm's teaching style isn't bad per se, but it's almost like you need to be accustomed to what he's talking about before you get there. He just starts lecturing and doesn't really explain what he's doing. It's difficult to follow in lectures just because he explains things in a weird way. Class is super test-heavy. Be ready to program python.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think I learned more in this course than any other course. Homework assignments were good, and only a few needed to be handed in. Textbook was excellent. Rahms examples added to the textbook explanations using his own understanding, and not just a repeat. Expect to read the textbook, though. A bit disorganized, but he makes up for it.

Prof. Rahm is awesome. Does a great job explaining concepts and makes his test reviews similar enough to the tests that you don't feel surprised by anything on the tests if you've done the reviews. Also a really funny guy and happy to answer any questions. Make sure to go to class though. The topics are complicated and become difficult if you skip.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lectures can be extremely confusing and make the material hard to understand at times. Tests are 80% identical to the practice test he gives you, so if you can do it over and over the tests are "easy" As. Class is difficult regardless, but this professor makes the most of it if you engage with the material.

This guy made this advance math class (pdes)easy to understand and do. Homework was only 4 problems a week and his test were near exactly like the practice, and it was take home, but prob because it was online and summer. His lectures are easy to understand and help w/ hw. Overall really caring, def take him instead of others.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Rahm is a very reasonable and chill guy. Very fun lectures and he knows what he's talking about. Works hard to give students their best fighting chance. Reviews were exactly like the exams. Doesn't try to trip you up with anything. Do the homework problems, do the reviews, and keep up with the class and you'll do fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Rahm grades nicely, however, his tests are tough. He does the WIR & posts review guides. Use those, maybe print out the blank notes before class, and you will do well. Try not to skip class, and do not be discouraged if you do not follow sometimes because he goes over proofs and does lots of algebra in class.

If someone is negative about this guy, it's because they genuinely didn't try to pass Diff Eq with him. Rahm is honestly the funniest and one of the best profs you could take. He really knows his stuff and there was never a lecture that I didn't enjoy. His projects are doable and his homeworks are fine, so no need to worry about those. Take him!!
Apart from being pretty funny, Professor Rahm genuinely cares about students learning the material. His supplemental videos helped tremendously and he also has the best exams reviews at TAMU.

Dr. Rahm is a great option for MATH 308. He teaches a very hard class so you should be prepared to attend every lecture and take lots of notes, but his explanations are very clear and he really helps you understand the material. His homeworks and exam reviews are also very helpful tools that make your life way easier when studying for his tests.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is understand and willing to admit his faults (I-D10-T error) and is good in office hours

Is overall a good professor. He is decent at teaching and sometimes will rush, but when you talk with him one on one or review the lectures and materials before class it's much easier. He is understanding about your grade and will work with you to make sure you understand the material to do better.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice guy, speaks clearly, and gives good hw assignments that help. His lectures are a bit rushed and frantic, often not stopping for questions or to clarify things. He seems too concerned with getting through the material to truly explain it when needed. Decent prof, but you'll have to review things a lot to understand.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: To give an idea of the level of quality, by the third week of class I stopped attending lectures and just taught myself using the textbook. He is great outside of class, but his lectures only serve to confuse you. Still, he was always helpful outside of class, but I would still steer clear if you can. (Unless you like teaching yourself)

Dr. Rahm's Calc 3 was a wonderful class-- I found myself learning a lot, and, I found myself not having to go far beyond what Dr. Rahm gave us to do well in the class. Specifically, the homework, lectures, textbook, and test-reviews made Calc 3 with Dr. Rahm a very non-stressful experience. And, his sense of humor made lectures easier to follow.

Professor Rahm is a very caring and genuine guy. Be sure to pay attention to his lectures and DO the practice exams, they're almost identical to the tests, which are open note!! There is a large amount of homework to complete, but all are due before each test. VERY helpful and patient during office hours too; I respect the man.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had Rahm last sem. Would NOT recommend! His lectures are frantic, flustered, and confusing. He often wrote wrong equations & formulas on the board and then corrected it 10 minutes later after going through several example problems with incorrect material. Hard to follow. Overall, nice guy though. Lectures, hw, and tests all seem unrelated.

He is a very nice guy and enjoys teaching. However, he teaches very technically with variables you've never seen before and will never see again. I get very confused in lecture so had to hire a tutor. Lots of homework but it is pretty simple. The tests are pretty tough, even being open notes.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took Professor Rahm for differential equations online. His tests were very similar to his test reviews. He was very understanding when it came to test difficulty and making a fair test at the end of the day. I really recommend taking him.

Absolutely atrocious of a math professor. This guy has his exams to be structured like a coding class and does not allow us to submit a written copy. Overall his class notes are a bunch of chicken scratch and never show quality examples.

Nice guy mostly, encourage nice learning environment. HOWEVER, make a ton of mistakes on his own examples, loads of worthless hw that wont get you anywhere nor does it prepare you for his exams. Exams weren't that hard. Boring lectures, I just skipped towards the end. Overall, I don't think I learned that much in lectures. Terrible prof, nice guy

Robert Rahm was honestly a nice guy. He responds to emails quickly and if you ever have trouble with turning something in on time he will help. That being said, as a professor he really confused me and I did not always understand his lectures. I needed to study a lotttt for this class but if you do the homework and test reviews you should be ok.

He was not my favorite professor. Never gave the right answer the first time - once took like four emails to tell us what sections were going to be on the test. He started doing these dumb "clicker" questions ( a google form) for more class participation, but in reality just ate time up. I just studied the homework problems and the review for tests

Occasionally pushes due dates back on homeworks. Tests are 80% of your grade but they're not bad as long as you do his practice tests, which are almost identical to his actual test. The main difference between his practice tests and actual tests are the numbers. Good at explaining things. Has a decent sense of humor.

Throughout the whole semester he kept changing how he structured his class and it was very frustrating. Although his class is not hard, his lectures are horrible. Not only does it confuse me , he gives wrong answers to questions and it confused me. At the end, I just stopped showing up to class.

this dude no teach he just be angry all time he is a man of god tho he be giving those easy tests. literally just show up and get an a. practice tests are the actual tests. he be lookin good tho ish final was peculiar

Not a bad person however he is a bad teacher. In class he doesn't teach concepts or the materials at all, instead he only does practice problems and usually gives the wrong answer. His lectures are not worth going and his notes are poorly written. Unless you're good at teaching yourself, I would suggest finding another professor to take instead.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His tests are very similar to the test reviews. He doesn't always answer his email and some days is a little unorganized however he is a reasonable professor.

He isnt the best teacher but his tests were very fair. take him hes the best for cal three, gives the best exams. my friends that had other profs struggled pretty hard, I studied the night before and got a's

He is not only easy, but he is so easy to follow. He has practice exams that are exactly the same or identical to his exams. I would recommend him because his notes are clear and his lectures are clear. Take him.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is easy as the tests/quizzes came verbatim from the homework/reviews. He is really nice, but doesn't stick to the schedule very well and ended up cancelling some of our computer projects. But he worked it out with students so nobody's grade was hurt by this. He also spent too much time on derivations though and was a bit confusing.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy if you just took the time to teach yourself the homework and the test reviews (tests were straight from the reviews and quizzes straight from HW). He is not a great teacher by any measure but the class is easy due to easy tests. No need for a textbook. Would take again.

Dr. Rahm was an extremely kind professor and person. Not the best at teaching the material and youd often find yourself leaving the class lost. However, his test and quizzes were extremely fair being that they drew exactly from his reviews and there were no curveballs. Overall, one of the better Diff Eq profs compared to what you hear from others.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Rob was a very sweet prof and as a person, he is great. As a MATH 308 teacher, not so much. The first month was very easy because he took much longer than other profs to teach basic concepts. Since it was his first semester teaching the course, everything was a bit awry. Our tests weren't that difficult but because he didn't teach, they were tough.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He has a great personality, but he is not the teacher to take if you never took Calculus in high school. He spends much of lecture doing proofs instead of teaching test material. Most math 152 teachers will provide an outline of the notes that you can print out ahead of class, but he does not. His explanations are confusing even in office hours.

I don't recommend taking Rahm. He pushed off our second test by 3 weeks, was always late to get stuff back to us and had two MATLAB projects that truly had nothing to do w/ the class. The lectures never really taught anything everyone struggled to teach themselves outside of class! Do the hw and reviews they are VERY helpful for tests & quizzes
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: It's important to note that during this semester, Dr. Rahm was sort of test running the course. He inverted the lesson plan for 308 to put the hardest material in the middle of the class, which I think works well. Tests aren't unreasonable, projects aren't bad, just do the homework!! Future classes would be lucky to have him.

Everybody I knew in MATH 308 would say "oh you're the class whos behind." The reason for us being behind was Rahm's lack of understanding of how to teach outside of his terms. We had two coding projects that used MATLAB in this class that weren't applicable to the material. I dont have enough space to tell my regret taking this class.

Rob is a really nice guy but not a great professor. He's young and inexperienced and it shows in the way he teaches the class. He wastes time doing proofs only to later admit that there is an easier way of doing things than the way he shows us. If you take him, be ready to figure things out on your own.

Rob's lectures are a bit weird, more focused on theoretical matters than actual practical application. The lecture is more of a very shallow introduction on how to use formulas and all your practical application and learning comes from recitation.

Rahm is a funny professor at times and a good man, but his lectures are tedious and filled with proofs; precious few actual problems from reviews or old tests are done during his lectures. He is well-learned but teaches more theory than is necessary for an engineering calculus class where practical calculus applications would be much more relevant.

Dr. Rahm's lectures were a bit random and not the best. He seemed to be worried about making mistakes during lecture which would cause him to make mistakes. However, his exam questions were taken straight from the optional homework so it wasn't hard to get a good grade. There are also daily quizzes which aren't hard if you do the homework before.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Rahm has a very laid back teaching style and cracks jokes all the time. the class is 4 tests and weekly homework. He moves homework back all the time for almost any excuse. He gives a review before the test that is very similar to the test. He gives you the option of completing the homework, if it helps your grade he'll count it, and if not he wont

He is one of the easier profs I have ever had. He does a pretty decent job of explaining the material, but he is kind of a mess. His tests are almost exactly like his practice tests, so as long as you do the homework and practice tests, you should be okay in the class.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Rahm is awesome! He gives out practice tests before each exam that are basically the same as the test. He even tells you the practice exam is harder than the actual test. He also has a funny sense of humor and is very straight forward to learn from. Easy A if you do the practice exams, highly recommend for calc 3!

Very straight-forward about material on test. Gives test reviews over the material and doesn't try and trick you but actually see if you know how to do the problems. Funny sense of humor and even brought his kid to class one time (pretty hilarious). Cares about his students and holds review sessions. Definitely recommend taking him for Cal 3.
